key_insight: A multi-objective Pareto-front optimization framework generates content-adaptive, quality-monotonic bitrate ladders for VVC by jointly optimizing bitrate, perceptual quality, and decoding complexity, enabling more efficient, device-aware adaptive streaming.
problem_solved: How to automatically build bitrate ladders for VVC that balance competing objectives (bitrate, video quality, and decoding complexity) in a content- and codec-dependent way while preserving monotonic quality progression across operating points.
method: Formulate joint multi-objective optimization over bitrate, perceptual quality (e.g., VMAF/PSNR) and decoding complexity to capture trade-offs.
Compute Pareto-fronts per content segment/title and select quality-monotonic operating points to form content-adaptive bitrate ladders.
Integrate complexity-aware constraints and selection rules into the VVC streaming workflow to pick ladder points suitable for diverse devices and network conditions.
impact: Provides a practical, data-driven way to incorporate resource constraints into streaming optimization — useful for ML practitioners designing codec control, perceptual metrics, or resource-aware deployment policies to maximize perceived quality per bit and reduce device compute/energy.
visual_elements: Pareto-front plot (2D or 3D) showing trade-offs among bitrate, quality, and decoding complexity with selected ladder points highlighted.
Bitrate-ladder diagram per content illustrating quality-monotonic progression and chosen operating points across network profiles.
Optimization pipeline flowchart (metrics extraction → Pareto-front computation → ladder selection → integration into streaming).
Heatmap or bar chart comparing perceptual quality vs bitrate and complexity across content types (demonstrating gains/trade-offs).
paper_title: Multi-Objective Pareto-Front Optimization for Efficient Adaptive VVC Streaming
paper_authors: Angeliki Katsenou, Vignesh V. Menon, Guoda Laurinaviciute, Benjamin Bross, Detlev Marpe
